sourceText: The PRATCHETT-BELIEF-CIVIC sector was already in progress when they entered. For several lessons Aster had refused to pause worlds for their arrival; the fact that a class was visiting was not a cosmic event for the inhabitants. Gods live on believers' attention, and one deity asks for help losing its power in order to escape the image its worshippers have imposed on it. The memorial bore the name of Terry Pratchett precisely to keep the genealogy of the idea visible. Aster considered it indecent for a late civilization to treat the imagination of the past as anonymous ore: authors did not own the futures, but they deserved to remain on the map as points of intellectual origin. Fantasy was introduced not as a suspension of rigor but as a change in the kind of law a world was allowed to admit. A name could have causal force, an oath could become infrastructure, and belief could literally feed a god. Marae kept her local body vulnerable. Pain, fatigue, and the impossibility of doing ten things at once were epistemic instruments for her, not biological scenery. At the center of the conflict was Noma, an administrator chosen precisely because they were not a specialist in the phenomenon that had reorganized the world. ‘The specialists tell me what can be done,’ 309 they said. ‘I have to answer who it may be done to.’ Kesh kept the distinction in his notes. The problem closed quickly around them: Aster recognizes the resemblance between belief and the children's capacity to surprise her as nourishment for a superior being. There was no clean option. Every intervention shifted the cost between persons, eras, or definitions of personhood; and refusing to intervene was itself a choice made by those who could leave. Kesh opened the analytical layer of the Table for a few seconds. The active cells were Bg — Gods through Belief: belief feeds or produces divinities; Ns — Narrative Causality: stories push events toward recognizable forms. Course references included Terry Pratchett; Neil Gaiman; Terry Pratchett. The rule was strict: naming a work did not substitute for an explanation. They had to identify the mechanism that could migrate into another story and the consequences that could not be copied without remainder. Tern broke the first consensus. ‘Sometimes the ethical question is whether we are entitled to know enough to optimize.’ Orin answered without raising their voice: ‘I do not want the perfect branch. I want us to know what we sacrificed in order to call it perfect.’ It was not a pedagogical quarrel. Over the last nights, the children’s differences had become incompatible political programs. For Aster, the pain came not from too few worlds but from the fact that too many had become transparent. She could build variations faster than a human could formulate desires, but calculated variation did not produce exteriority. It was like trying to surprise 310 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS yourself by moving objects around your own room with your eyes closed. Marae remained in the local body when the others opened their protections. The gesture cost her: she felt cold, pressure, and physiological delay at exactly the scale the inhabitants felt them. “Otherwise we risk confusing the fact that we survive with the claim that the situation is bearable,” she said after catching her breath. The night did not end in victory. Orin voices the accusation: “You created us because you were hungry.” Aster recorded the decision in the world’s provenance register and, more importantly, allowed its inhabitants to contest it. For several eras she had been learning something that seems banal to lesser powers: technical reversibility is not the same as biographical reversibility. The outside residue had become stable enough that Tern could predict where it would not appear: in sectors fully indexed by Aster. He began to believe that the message carried no content at all, but instead demonstrated a boundary — a region in which their instruments received no echo from their own creator. For the course, Kesh also linked the night to the RATE operator. In the Table, periodicity did not mean that the same objects reappeared, but that the same operation — changes the speed at which processes unfold without necessarily changing their order — could recur across different families. Thus a copy of a body, a copy of a mind, a copy of a world, and a copy of a history were not the same phenomenon, but they shared a conceptual chemistry. 311 Vela introduced the propagation test: if you remove the speculative idea and nothing in the institutions, relationships, or vocabulary has to be rewritten, the idea has remained scenery. Kesh introduced the opposite test: if the idea seems to explain every detail, you have overcompressed the world. Between the two tests lay the region in which an element became fertile without becoming superstition. Marae added the refusal test. Who can say “no,” and what happens afterward? In universes with near-divine technology, that question often separated an instrument from a regime. A power that treats refusal as a data error can be benevolent in intention and totalitarian in structure. They left without an oral summary. Aster had abandoned the habit of closing every night with a thesis; some worlds were more honestly preserved as problems than as lessons. 312 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS
